title: Positive shift for threshold signs
statement: Let $\alpha$ be a finite set, let $f:\alpha\to\{ -1,1\}$, and let $p:\alpha\to\mathbb R$ satisfy $f(x)=1$ when $p(x)\geq 0$ and $f(x)=-1$ when $p(x)<0$. There is a real number $c>0$ such that $f(x)(p(x)+c)>0$ for every $x\in\alpha$.
hypotheses_covered: At every $x$, $f(x)$ is the threshold sign determined by whether $p(x)\geq0$
